99.t: Teaching himself the fingering, his embouchure, and C versus do-re-mi
99.s: He works out fingerings from a chart the first night, never learns the orthodox embouchure, and discovers the difference between vocal and instrumental note names.
99.q: So, as they -- as the saxophone -- I noticed the guys, they were -- these three fingers would be down -- and these three fingers would be down, and this right finger would be down and that would be do. And as they would raise the finger up, do re -- as they raised the finger up, it was just a…

99.t: Studying alone from the instruction book after Beam refuses to teach him
99.s: He sacrifices pleasures to learn, is told by Beam he cannot be taught because he is colored, and works through band music one bar at a time.
99.q: And so, I bent myself in that book every morning and every night. The people in the community were mad with me, and they called me everything but child of God. (unintelligible). Even my father got sick of me around the house. And my mother would tell my dad, 'Leave him alone. Leave him alone.'

99.t: A white teacher tries to swap horns
99.s: A Little Rock saxophone teacher tries to trade his blue 'jazz' sax for Pillars's horn, so Pillars stops taking lessons.
99.q: That was because they couldn't play saxophone at all. They couldn't play saxophone, and they didn't know as much about it as I did. But what happened, there was -- I found there was a white teacher that taught saxophone and lived in Little Rock. I contacted him. I went to him and took one lesson.…

99.t: Alvin Fat Walls and the dignity of dinner music
99.s: He plays second sax beside virtuoso Alvin Fat Walls and learns how to play soft, well-mannered dinner and luncheon music.
99.q: Okay. I joined the Gordon C. Harrison Band. We had two saxophones. The first saxophonist's name was Alvin Fat Walls. Alvin Fat Walls was a virtuoso on the

864.t: Navy clarinet and lessons with Tio and others
864.s: He got a clarinet in Bordeaux while in the Navy, then after 1921 took lessons from several teachers including the younger Lorenzo Tio.
864.q: I happened to meet one of his brothers over in Bordeaux, France. Well, he had one of John's old clarinets and just had it laying up there. And I told him, I said, well, you got that horn, why don't you give it to me? You ain't using it. For sure enough, he did. And I took John's clarinet and kept…

765.t: Starting Fazola on clarinet and saxophone with Dan Sanderson
765.s: Schiro taught Fazola fingering; both studied with Professor Sanderson, Fazola progressed fast and added many instruments.
765.q: We used to make the homebrew joints and all, and the fine, and the Arcadia, the Levita and all. We used to listen to him, and I showed him the finger on my old Albus system that I had. And this side of the week, he started learning the whole thing. You know what I mean? He was really good at it.…

187.t: Williams's teaching of breathing, and his son George and daughter Bella
187.s: Williams taught breath control; son George was a multi-instrumentalist and Bella a pianist.
187.q: Yeah, on how to take the breath. How to take your breath. Filling up the stomach. Filling up the stomach, surely, yeah. Just like those fellas who hold that note so long, you know? Yeah. That's what he was teaching me that.

296.t: First instrument alto; teacher Charles Sio of the French Opera
296.s: He began on alto; his teacher Charles Sio played in the French Opera band. The group struggles to identify the teacher's woodwind instrument.
296.q: There was about three, four of them in the band.

439.t: Classical teacher Eva Wasserman and saxophone ideas on clarinet
439.s: Her classical teacher supported her move to jazz; her sax studies and Illinois Jacquet shaped her clarinet playing.
439.q: Well my classical teacher, I had one main teacher when I was, before I transformed into jazz life, when I was studying a little bit of classical clarinet and her name is Eva Wasserman, she still lives in Israel. And she has been very supportive of my path and she calls me up and she’s proud of me,…

216.t: Classical teachers and keeping jazz separate
216.s: His classical teachers were liberal; he played clarinet legit and jazz on saxophone.
216.ch: Denver youth and University of Denver
216.q: No. They were pretty liberal. Yeah. They were pretty liberal even though they were straight ahead classical teachers and performers, they didn’t give me a hard time about it. I think I mainly kept things separated. You know I mean I played Dixieland clarinet and all that kind of stuff, but I never…

85.t: Early teachers: Proctor, Eugene Michaels, Rudy Powell and Arthur Reeves
85.s: He names his teachers and says Arthur Reeves shaped his sound, and mentions the Vereecken saxophone method.
85.q: Actually, the teacher that he recommended first was a professor, Eugene Michaels, who had been in the army or whatever service, some military service, and, considering I was a beginner, he had his assistant teach me and spend as much time with me as Professor Michaels himself did. His assistant was…

641.t: First lesson at Picou's house and his fame for High Society
641.s: Picou first shooed Joe away, then gave him a little book; his fame rested on playing High Society.
641.q: Like Jelly Roll. But I remember the first time he said, "You be at my house at..." My sister lived on Hillary and Saint Bernard in New Orleans, and I could walk to his house where he was living, and that day... The first day he told me to come around there at around 3 o'clock, and I knocked on the…

91.t: Saxophone teachers Eugene Mikell and Arthur Reeves
91.s: He studied with Mikell, Rudy Powell and then Arthur Reeves, who stressed tone, sound and intonation.
91.q: And then I went to a teacher named Michael -- what was his first name? Eugene. Yes. And I studied with him for a while; he also had 2 sons who were fine musicians -- Otto and Gene Jr. After studying with him a while, he turned me over -- well, at the beginning, he turned me over to who was his star…
